reviewer: Codex LLM-assisted source, written-work, and submitted-evidence review; TA verification pending
canvas_summary: The newly uploaded ETL scripts meet the source-level Task 2 and Task 3 requirements. Remaining deductions are for IAM boundaries, lifecycle durations, lineage labels, and README content.
review_notes: Applied the TA-supplied older Task 2.3 criterion: grade the Glue module and clean crawler/job apply; do not deduct this row for a private connection or separately committed script source.

TA regrade applies the no-saved-output rule to T3.4 as well: no deduction solely for the absent feature job-run file when the job is configured and apply completed; runtime status remains unverified offline.

Restored the remaining T1.4 point because the LocalStack Terraform apply created all three IAM roles and the VPC with NAT disabled; the later awslocal verification could not run because awslocal was not installed.

Restored the T1.1 point deducted for the missing self-referencing security-group ingress: the scored T1.1 criterion is private subnet, NAT, and Domain relocation, and the TA-supplied older Task 2.3 rubric excludes private Glue networking from that score.

Regraded Task 2 and Task 3 after the Python sources were added. Static review awards full T2.2, T3.1, and T3.2 credit: types/date parsing, median and unknown imputation, transaction_id deduplication, fixed observation/outcome windows, customer-level RFM, tiers, bounded churn proxy, and outcome-derived label are implemented. T3.4 remains full under the TA no-saved-output ruling because the feature job is configured and the submitted apply completed; no AWS job was run as part of this regrade.

Deployment follow-up: glue-scripts/transform.py and glue-scripts/feature_engineer.py are present, but infrastructure/modules/glue/main.tf references cs401r-lab2-template/glue-scripts/ for both source and filemd5. That directory is absent in the current repo; a fresh apply may fail or not use these newly added files. This is reported as implementation feedback and did not reduce the source-code rubric rows.

T1.1.reason: The submitted source and verification evidence establish the private subnet, guarded NAT, and SageMaker Domain relocation required for T1.1. The missing self-referencing ingress is not included in this scored criterion, and private Glue networking is excluded under the TA-supplied older Task 2.3 rubric.

T1.2.reason: All three roles exist, but MLEngineer can write processed/ and DataEngineer can write artifacts/glue/; those grants exceed the handout's required write boundaries.

T1.3.reason: Five lifecycle rules are present, but every retention period differs from the required 90/30/30/60/7-day values.

T1.4.reason: The LocalStack Terraform apply completed, creating all three IAM roles and the VPC; the local environment disables NAT. The subsequent awslocal verification stopped only because the awslocal executable was unavailable.

T2.1.reason: The Terraform configuration defines the catalog database and raw/customers crawler. Under the older rubric supplied by the TA, get-table had to return a schema, but saving its output was not required. The absent verifier file alone is not deducted; the historical table result cannot be independently confirmed offline.

T2.2.reason: The newly submitted transform.py casts the nine schema fields, trims and converts blanks to nulls, parses ISO and MM/dd/yyyy dates, drops null customer IDs, imputes numeric medians and string unknowns, and deduplicates by transaction_id with an ordering rule. Source-level requirements are met.

T2.3.reason: The Glue module defines the crawler and transform job, and the committed extension log shows a clean apply creating the crawler and jobs. Under the older rubric supplied by the TA, this row scores module presence and a clean crawler/job apply; script source/upload and private NETWORK connection are outside this row.

T2.4.reason: The Terraform configuration defines the transform job and the saved apply log records a clean apply. The older rubric required get-job-run to return SUCCEEDED but did not require saving that output. No verifier result is available to independently confirm the historical run; absence of the output file alone is not deducted.

T3.1.reason: The newly submitted feature_engineer.py implements the five required stages: fixed temporal split, customer-level RFM aggregates, loyalty tiers, bounded scaled churn proxy, and label derived from holdout activity. It also checks nulls, risk bounds, tier coverage, and output writing. Source-level feature requirements are met.

T3.2.reason: The feature script uses fixed FEATURE_CUTOFF and SNAPSHOT dates, computes features from history at or before the cutoff, and derives churn_label only from purchases in the subsequent outcome window. This establishes the required temporal separation statically; no AWS output was run during this regrade.

T3.3.reason: The Terraform Feature Group defines all 16 required names and types, including Fractional event_time and Integral churn_label, with online and offline stores.

T3.4.reason: The Terraform module defines the feature-engineering job, and the saved apply log shows a clean apply. Under the TA direction applying the legacy no-saved-output rule to T3.4, absence of a committed feature job-run result is not deducted. The historical SUCCEEDED state is not independently verifiable offline.

T4.1.reason: The contract identifies producer and consumers, states transaction grain, lists nine typed columns with nullability, at least three measurable guarantees, a two-hour freshness target, and a new-prefix/five-business-day breaking-change policy.

T4.2.reason: The diagram includes the major source-to-Feature-Store nodes and CSV/Parquet/PutRecord labels, but none of its write edges identifies the IAM writer.

T5.1.reason: Glue and Feature Store have separate Terraform modules wired from the dev environment without conflicting duplicate resources.

T5.2.reason: New Glue and Feature Store resource names use project/environment variables or module inputs instead of fixed deployed names.

T5.3.reason: The offline Terraform format check passed, and the committed successful apply provides historical configuration evidence without accessing AWS.

T5.4.reason: The committed extension log records a successful Terraform apply involving the SageMaker Domain.

T5.5.reason: The README contains only a title, with no Lab 2 additions or run sequence.
